checks.question: Are author-tool dependencies separate from production apps and public tarballs usable without private VM packages?
checks.detail: CLI depends on public SDK/testkit and fixed tools. Boundary gate passes. Installed tarballs have no workspace source alias/private VM dependency and public host/type smoke succeeds. This is bounded artifact/dependency evidence.

checks.question: Do selected source bytes, inert config and same-VM guest tests prevent Node execution of project code?
checks.detail: Root/file identities, link/path checks, bounded JSON, import allowlist and owned source/assets precede fixed configFile:false/envDir:false build. Sources and tests execute in testkit VM. Sealed-source mutation, config/hook fixtures and a tsconfig field-semantics probe pass.

checks.question: Does file sealing retain memory proportional to selected contents while archive/sign failures remain bounded and fail closed?
checks.detail: B17-C01: each asset slice retains its entire 8 MiB + 1 backing buffer. A valid 33-asset snapshot contains 455 bytes but retains 276824097 backing bytes. Deterministic repack/signature and .pem rejection otherwise pass; unreviewed exceptional key-file IO cases remain explicit limits.

checks.question: Are diagnostic data redacted and malformed configuration distinguished from environment failure?
checks.detail: B17-C02: null configuration reaches Object.keys without an object guard, producing TOOL_FAILURE / exit 3 instead of CONFIG / exit 2. Guest-thrown details, local paths and key-marker bytes remain absent from tested diagnostics.

checks.question: Do tested artifacts carry licenses and avoid implying registry publication or native admission?
checks.detail: All three tarballs carry package/LICENSE; testkit includes binding/QuickJS licenses. Four off-repository templates pass installation, same-VM runtime/type smoke, repack/verify/migration. Self-signatures remain unverified publishers and local outputs do not claim publication/admission.

findings.title: Small sealed files retain full per-file budget buffers
findings.trigger: A project declares multiple small assets, each read with the default 8 MiB asset budget.
findings.effect: openProject.read returns Buffer.subarray from an 8 MiB + 1 allocation. Snapshot.assets keeps the backing stores alive through build/test/pack/DEV. Small valid projects incur hundreds of MiB of retained external backing memory; at the allowed 100 assets this approaches 800 MiB even for tiny content.
findings.measurementLimit: This measures retained unique ArrayBuffer.byteLength, not RSS, physical-memory commitment, peak process memory or an observed OOM.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Copy the returned used bytes into content-sized storage or use an identity-checked bounded read sized to the observed regular file; retain growth/change detection and add a tiny-multi-asset regression. Consider the total snapshot budget separately.

findings.title: Null JSON configuration is reported as an environment failure
findings.trigger: A selected project has plugin.config.json containing valid JSON null; run am-plugin check or pack.
findings.effect: Object.keys(config) throws before the CONFIG Diagnostic is created. CLI returns code 3 / TOOL_FAILURE, although its documented unsupported-config path returns code 2. Automation cannot distinguish author input error from environment failure.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Validate that parsed configuration is a non-null object of the supported shape before enumerating or reading fields, and add a CLI black-box malformed-config exit-code regression.
